lines: Back without a dent worth naming. I'll call that a good fit.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I'll count that as good work.
Following you taught me that plans sound much safer before anyone starts walking.
I kept up, mostly. My feet have a harsher opinion of the trip.
Next time, warn me before the road becomes a test of character.
I learned two things out there, stay close, and ask better questions earlier.
You move like danger is a normal part of the route. I am still adjusting to that.
It was not all bad. Some views are worth sore legs and nervous glances.
If I followed you again, I would pack more food and fewer assumptions.
I came home with only sore feet.
Every plate returned in one piece.
The village appeared before worry did.
The road left dust and no wounds.
I heard the forge from the last hill.
No repairs are needed today.
The route was kinder than expected.
Home has never looked sturdier.
I trusted you and returned safely.
That journey ended well.
There are marks on me I would rather see on a breastplate. Next time, let the metal take it.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
The armor missed one painful gap.
The plate will mend before the bruise.
The trip cost more than planned.
Watch the danger next time.
My gear returned better than I did.
The healer scolded both of us.
I know where the journey failed.
Worse was possible, but this hurts.
My ribs remember the story.
Do not call this a scratch.
I need rest before another road.
The wound has its own schedule.
A warning could have prevented this.
I came back walking, barely.
Next time the metal takes the blow.
I should have stopped sooner.
I will not rush recovery.
I know the sound of a bad strike. Yours was worse because I trusted the hand behind it.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
You knew where the armor opened.
I expected danger ahead, not beside me.
The wound healed cleaner than trust.
A chosen strike is no accident.
I watched the road while you turned.
Armor cannot stop broken promises.
I would have guarded your back.
You used trust as a weak point.
I came home believing less.
Keep your distance now.
Your voice sounds different to me.
The road was safer than my guide.
I remember the hand behind the blow.
Do not ask me to follow again.
Metal is easier to repair.
You made the walk home longer.
That mark will outlast the bruise.
A boat carries armor poorly, but it carried me well enough.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
The boat brought us home dry.
Armor belongs on steady ground.
Each wave questioned my trade.
I held the rail all crossing.
The water was calm. I was not.
Land felt wonderfully still.
I will pack less iron next time.
We never tested whether mail floats.
The hull creaked under my boots.
The dock looked beautiful.
I sat where the armor allowed.
The oarsman laughed at my balance.
My gear gained boat scratches.
The river saved us walking.
I disliked every splash.
Nothing came over the side.
Water travel makes fear feel slow.
